newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stock market unnerved by record day drop.
newsitem.headline: Manila stock market unnerved by record day drop.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange index suffered its biggest-ever single-day drop on Monday, shattering market confidence and leading to predictions that share prices will fall further.
The main index fell 110 points, or nearly four percent, to 2,852.16.
It had been trending downward since the beginning of the month and many analysts had expressed hope last week that the market had touched bottom.
But Monday's slump below the key 2,900 support level has convinced many analysts the gloom would persist.
"Corporate earnings are the culprits this time. In a situation like this, any bad news is seen as an opportunity to sell," said Joel Santillan, chief analyst at Asian Oceanic Merit Securities.
"We suspect another down move tomorrow as people are still jittery and are rethinking their positions," he said.
On Friday, shares of Philippine National Bank, the country's largest bank, plummeted by 21 percent to 410 pesos per share after it reported lower-than- expected profits.
PNB's results were the worst among top companies since the reporting season for nine-month earnings began last week.
Another major stock, Pilipino Telephone Corp, or Piltel, fell more than four percent on Monday to 23 pesos per share.
Piltel, a subsidiary of blue-chip Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, had reported a 27 percent jump in profit in the first nine months to 722.4 million pesos.
That figure also was lower than forecast due to losses from illegal phone calls. Piltel officials later on Monday cut the company's full-year profit forecast.
Analysts said the poor showings by the two companies should not have pushed the market down so sharply as most other company results have met expectations.
"The market has once again overreacted," said Raul Ruiz, vice-president at Sun Hung Kai Securities Inc.
When the current bear phase began in the first week of October, many had blamed the sell-off on foreign funds reallocating their portfolios.

Foreign funds account for more than 50 percent of the daily trading volume on the Philippine Stock Exchange and analysts said the funds often caused the market to move due to their tendency to concentrate on blue chips.

"We now see the unwanted effect of a strategy which entails that they (foreign funds) concentrate on a handful of stocks which carry the index. So when they sell there's a very rapid effect on the index," said Joey Salceda, director at SBC Warburg.
Analysts said a large initial public offering by Digital Telecommunication opening on Wednesday could further dampen the market.
The offering is aimed at raising over 3.0 billion pesos.
"It will siphon off liquidity and divide the attention of a market that's looking for short-term investments," Cilette Liboro, analyst at Citisecurities Inc said.
